context: The scene: a bandit (Gimblebock) is standing over one of his companions who has been crushed to death by a falling boulder amid the ruined chapel. He responds with shock and annoyance rather than grief, suggesting he thinks it was an accident but is more unnerved than sympathetic. This group are hardened criminals accustomed to corpses and violence — the area has seen other dying or trapped crew members and looted bodies, so death is treated pragmatically. You may have just emerged from the ruins, and the bandits were already worried about their friend inside, which explains their terse, unsentimental reaction.
